{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "sedited",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected that defaulting to check backportability causes failures when only verifying subtree integrity; questioned whether it solves a real problem"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Approach NACK; considers bash logic unnecessary maintenance overhead for a style preference"
    },
    {
      "login": "ryanofsky",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "ACKed; argued the check simplifies non-trivial verification and documents good backporting practice"
    },
    {
      "login": "BrandonOdiwuor",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "tested and ACKed"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:4936395031",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "usefulness",
      "text": "asks whether this solves a real problem given that commits from subtrees are sometimes cherry-picked when fixes need backporting",
      "quote": "We sometimes cherry-pick commits from the subtree if they contain fixes that need backporting. Is this really solving a problem?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "ryanofsky explained the PR addresses wider subtree bumps rather than isolated cherry-picks",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [
        "r:4996279203"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "r:4996279203",
      "status_by_quote": "This PR is primarily trying to address a different use-case, when there are wider improvements like stability fixes in the subtree that you want to backport to multiple release branches"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4936824044",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "warning on merge commits that adjust code could encourage build failures or warn unnecessarily when adjustments are required",
      "quote": "In some rare cases it is required to adjust the code for the subtree bump in the merge commit itself (to avoid build failures on the merge commit itself), so that would warn in that case and somehow encourage build failures?",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added --incompatible option to opt out of the check",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4937509996",
        "c:4937561579"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4995114634",
      "status_by_quote": "I did that in the last update commit... This way, each commit can opt-in or out, and enforce it. But :man_shrugging:"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4936824044",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "how does merging the same subtree commit as-is simplify backports compared to creating a second similar merge commit on the backport branch?",
      "quote": "can you explain how this simplifies \"backport\"? IIUC you are referring to merging the subtree merge commit as-is into several branches?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained that reusing the exact same merge commit hash makes backports trivial to review",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4937509996"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4937509996",
      "status_by_quote": "Yes, we've done this a few times for libmultiprocess: #34804 and #34952 have the exact same merge commit hash, making the pack-port trivial to review."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4790659090",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "use a stricter check (error instead of warning), clarify error messages and documentation, and inspect commits even when not checked out at HEAD",
      "quote": "I think having the warning is better than not having it, but a stricter approach would seem better here.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author adopted suggested changes in c:5102482210; ryanofsky ACKed update",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5102482210"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "r:4996279203",
      "status_by_quote": "Thanks for the updates. New commit split makes this easier to review and I think the script messages and documentation are easier to understand now."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4073574189",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "apply suggested checkout commands to developer-notes documentation to make instructions easy to copy-paste",
      "quote": "I think the suggested change should be applied. Otherwise, it is harder to copy-paste the instructions here and they'll have to be figured out fresh on each invocation.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author applied checkout instructions to doc/developer-notes.md",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4081544306"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4081544306",
      "status_by_quote": "Done"
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5767118616",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "default behavior causes git-subtree-check to fail on most subtrees for users who only want to verify subtree integrity",
      "quote": "The script without the extra argument fails on most subtrees and the exception is applied to the CI. My feeling is this is done the wrong way around. Somebody who just wants to verify subtree integrity does not care whether updates to the subtree are easier to backport.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author agreed to invert default if preferred, and ryanofsky explained rationale; sedited has not followed up",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5776628439"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:5778543666"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5776628439",
      "status_by_quote": "I would be fine with making `--incompatible` the default, if more people prefer that."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5780682848",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "adds unnecessary bash logic and maintenance overhead for what is a style preference that can be verified with git log or documentation",
      "quote": "I don't see why something so trivial needs so much code or even effort that all needs to be maintained in the future (like https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35980) ... Approach NACK",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "maflcko reaffirmed objection and reiterated NACK in c:5794085899 and c:5905591607 following author and reviewer replies",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5793387894"
      ],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:5901706481",
        "c:5913931461"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5905591607",
      "status_by_quote": "The more I think about this, the stronger my NACK gets and I am slowly leaning toward a wholesale concept NACK instead of an approach NACK."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:4790659090",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "having the warning is better than not having it, though a stricter approach would seem better",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": [
        "test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh",
        "doc/developer-notes.md"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4996279203",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "documents practice of basing new subtree updates on previous updates, allowing same commits to be merged into multiple branches and saving reviewer effort",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": [
        "test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh",
        "doc/developer-notes.md"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5003680532",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "tested that the new backportability check passes and errors as expected, and verified --incompatible suppresses the check",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "tested",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "deciding whether to proceed or adjust approach following maflcko's Approach NACK and sedited's feedback",
      "id": "c:5905591607"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Re-read conversion: changed r:4790659090 from objection to suggestion since ryanofsky approved the PR while suggesting improvements; added questions from c:4936395031 and c:4936824044; added suggestion rc:4073574189 which was addressed. Tracked maflcko's standing Approach NACK through c:5905591607."
}
